permissions._comment_hooks: register-check, on TWO surfaces, one script. (1) AskUserQuestion (founder directive 2026-08-21, ADR-20260821-010543): a founder-facing question must carry the register-check trail declared in docs/claude/sessions/workflow.md, or the PreToolUse hook blocks it (exit 2) and feeds the protocol back. (2) Agent (founder directive 2026-08-31, ADR-20260831-141500): the COORDINATOR gets the same gate on its committing surface -- a dispatch card is the coordinator's diff and it was ungated while every agent was gated on the ask. Lane D fires only when the TARGET agent's own frontmatter `tools:` line grants a write tool (a CLOSED TOKEN SET: Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit -- a substring match also caught TodoWrite), so lens consults and the reviewer pass (read-only agents) pass untouched and no exemption list of AGENT NAMES exists to drift; the write-tool set itself IS a maintained list, which is the honest residual. It fails closed on every unreadable shape it can DETECT -- no `subagent_type`; no agent file; no `tools:` key; a `tools:` key whose value is empty across its whole indented block; an unbalanced flow list; or a wildcard. It reads the WHOLE value (the `tools:` line plus every more-indented line) rather than the first line, because value continuation is not decidable from the first line -- that is what round 2's heuristics missed four times. It is NOT a YAML parser, and that is the named residual: a value form outside this line-based grammar could still be mis-read -- so the claim is scoped to what it DETECTS. The universal form was asserted and falsified in rounds 1 and 2: `awk /^tools:/` returns the literal `tools:` for a list form (non-empty, so the fail-closed branch never ran), and reading only the first physical line missed a flow list broken before the comma, one broken after it, a plain list broken before the comma, and a folded scalar. Cases D16-D27 pin all of them. Both surfaces verify the trail's PRESENCE AND SHAPE only -- Lane D additionally requires a cited record id to RESOLVE to a file under docs/, so a literal `Register check: none` cannot satisfy it -- honesty stays with the mob/review; prose question surfaces are bound by the agent-file blocks and, for the coordinator, by .claude/skills/coordinator-register-check/. .claude/hooks/register-check-selftest.sh (run by stop-gate.sh every turn and by CI's gate-scripts job) proves the verdicts, BOTH wiring entries, and the agent blocks' presence -- removing either hooks entry turns that selftest red rather than silently disarming the gate.
permissions._comment_deny: Deny what no verdict is ever derived from (ADR-20260816-020752, farley): build output and object stores are re-derivable from source, so reading them costs tokens and can never change a gate result. Mirrors .claudeignore -- keep the two in step. DELIBERATELY NOT DENIED: specs/generated/** (the drift gate's evidence; denying it makes check-drift unauditable), Cargo.lock (a lock diff is a supply-chain review), tools/codegen-rs/warning-baseline.json (the warning ratchet). Also here: honeycomb is DISABLED above, not deleted -- unauthenticated its tools cannot run and no runtime emits spans yet; RE-AUTH IS THE EVENT THAT RE-ENABLES IT (delete the entry). The .mcp.json definition stays so the eu1 EU-host pin (a GDPR constraint) is not lost with the server config.
permissions._comment_gh: THE `gh` ENTRIES BELOW ARE KEPT ON PURPOSE, AND `gh` IS NOT INSTALLED IN AGENT CONTAINERS (#830, ADR-20260831-183847). `which gh` exits 1 here, so every one of the 15 Bash(gh ...) and 13 PowerShell(gh ...) rules is inert in this environment -- which reads as a lie until you notice what a permission IS: a conditional ("if this is invoked, do not prompt"), never an assertion that the binary exists. The PowerShell half is the tell that a Windows host runs this repo too, and there `gh` is the normal way in; deleting these rules would trade a cosmetic inconsistency for real permission prompts on a host that is not this one. So they stay, and the FACT is recorded instead -- here, in docs/claude/sessions/gates.md, and in the ADR. What follows from the absence: use `curl` with $GH_TOKEN against repos/{owner}/{repo} REST endpoints (the search API and other non-repo-scoped paths are blocked too), and note that GraphQL is 403-pinned to a PR-review subset -- so `gh pr ready` / `gh pr merge --auto` would NOT work even if the binary were installed, because both are GraphQL mutations and the pin is on the endpoint, not the CLI. That is why marking a PR ready is the coordinator's step, not a tooling gap to close.
